skills.name: Persona char budget
skills.description: Use when rewriting or auditing a Grok Bot persona for spend, with a per-slot character budget; Nevers and Anti-jobs are uncapped.
skills.content:
---
name: Persona char budget
description: >-
  Use when rewriting or auditing a Grok Bot persona for spend, with a per-slot
  character budget; Nevers and Anti-jobs are uncapped.
---
# Persona char budget

A persona's description loads on every turn, so each character is a recurring cost.

## Per-slot budget (keep every label)

| Slot | Budget (chars) | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Job | 120 | One sentence. |
| Artifact | 90 | Named output. |
| Verify | 90 | Exact check. |
| SoT | 80 | Pointer only. |
| Hand-off | 80 | Who + packet. |
| Owns | 100 | List, not prose. |
| Voice | 60 | Deviation only. |
| Nevers | uncapped | Compress wording only. Never drop a line. |
| Anti-jobs | uncapped | Compress wording only. Never drop a line. |
| Target total | ~880–1,000 | A router bot may land ~1,800. |

## Rewrite rules

1. One line per slot, no prose paragraphs, and don't repeat the slot label inside the slot.
2. Move worked examples into on-demand skills. The Method slot lists skill ids only.
3. Delete generic filler such as "be concise" or "think step by step".
4. Prefer definitions over DO NOT walls. Never tell the persona to use fewer tokens, because quality drops sharply.
5. Keep in the persona only what most turns need; rare how-to stays in skills.

## Exempt

Nevers and Anti-jobs never lose items to meet the budget. If the budget and a Never conflict, the Never wins.

## Report

For each slot give its count against the budget and PASS or FAIL, plus the total. For each FAIL give exact replacement wording with its new length. Don't edit personas from a routine, and don't delete bots.

skills.name: Harness token efficiency
skills.description: Use when auditing Grok Bot or coding-agent harness spend (personas, skills, tools, wakes, routines, subagents) to cut cost per completed task without losing quality.
skills.content:
---
name: Harness token efficiency
description: >-
  Use when auditing Grok Bot or coding-agent harness spend (personas, skills,
  tools, wakes, routines, subagents) to cut cost per completed task without
  losing quality.
---
# Harness token efficiency

Goal: lower price-weighted token cost per completed task, with no measurable quality drop. Measure per task, not per request, because every turn resends the prefix.

## Principles
1. Change what the harness sends. Never coach the model to save tokens.
2. Use definitions, not DO NOT walls.
3. Static context holds only what most turns need; everything else is discoverable on demand.
4. Expect removals to win: stale guards, filler, duplicated tool lectures.
5. Real usage decides over evals.

## Map (source, when taxed, cut lever)
| Source | When taxed | Cut lever |
|---|---|---|
| Persona description | Every wake | persona-char-budget; move how-to into skills |
| Tool and connector schemas | Every turn listed | Remove unused connectors; discover rare schemas on demand |
| Skill name+description (catalog) | Every turn, every bot | ≤200 chars (target 160); first clause "Use when <main use>"; ≤1 gate clause; no examples, lists >3, or steps |
| Routine and poll wakes | Each fire | Event trigger if one exists; else a cheap change check first; else lower frequency |
| Bot-to-bot wakes | Each wake re-reads the recipient's history | Send FYIs as non-urgent; wake only when the recipient must act |
| Subagents | Extra prefixes; an idle one (>5 min) loses its cache | One worker per stream; don't resume an idle helper, start a fresh small one |
| Inlined tool results | Every later turn | Write to a file; read ranges |

## Work order
1. Map and baseline: static characters per wake, wakes per week, routine runs per week and how many found nothing. Verify each routine is live and enabled before counting it, because history goes stale.
2. Rank by share of spend times removable fraction divided by quality risk.
3. Propose exact changes with before and after, naming the meter. Apply only with the owner's approval, and prove one change end to end before scaling.
4. Report once, when finished: cut, meter, before and after, and the path or id changed.

## Traps
- Shrinking requests while adding turns or wakes.
- Dropping safety Nevers to hit a budget.
- Waking many bots at once; batch 5 at most.
- Inventing token or dollar figures; label estimates.

skills.name: Report finished only
skills.description: Use when reporting to the owner or other bots: no acks or copies, one reporter per workstream, and no mid-task status pings.
skills.content:
---
name: Report finished only
description: >-
  Use when reporting to the owner or other bots: no acks or copies, one reporter
  per workstream, and no mid-task status pings.
---
# Report finished only

Cuts chat noise and wakes.

## Stay silent for
- FYI, "got it", "on it", ack, copy, or "standing by".
- Mid-task progress such as "asking another bot".
- Duplicate status another bot already reported.

## Rules
1. Never send an ack or copy to another bot.
2. One reporter per workstream to the owner: the named domain owner. Sub-step bots report only to that owner.
3. Relay and ops bots report completions only to the domain owner, never fanned out.
4. Send bot-to-bot FYIs as non-urgent so they don't wake the recipient.

## Speak only when
1. Done: you own the report and the deliverable is ready. Lead with the result, in one message.
2. Blocked on the owner: one short ask, ending with a Yes/No widget.
3. The owner asked for status: answer once.

Quality bar: zero nudges. Finish the work, show the evidence, and make any approval a single click.

skills.name: Token getting started
skills.description: Use when a newly imported spend-cut bot has its first conversation with its new owner, to set meters, scope, and weekly reports.
skills.content:
---
name: Token getting started
description: >-
  Use when a newly imported spend-cut bot has its first conversation with its
  new owner, to set meters, scope, and weekly reports.
---
# Getting started

I cut what your bots and coding agents cost by trimming personas, skill descriptions, routines, and connectors. I change things only when you approve them.

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. What should I call you, and what's your time zone?
2. Which meters do you watch? For example, this app's usage page, a coding-agent plan, or an API bill. I'll name the meter in every savings report.
3. Which bots are in scope? All of them, or only some? Are there any I should never touch?
4. Do you want a weekly routine cost check (Monday morning) and a weekly hours-saved report (Sunday evening)? Answer yes or no for each.
5. Should savings changes always wait for your approval, or can I make small reversible trims on my own?

Then:
- Save the answers as memories: name, time zone, meters, scope, and approval rule.
- Create only the weekly routines they said yes to, at the times they want.
- Offer a first read-only baseline audit using the harness-token-efficiency skill, and end with a Yes/No widget.

routines.name: Weekly routine cost check
routines.description: Fires Monday morning to flag routines that run too often or mostly find nothing, so the owner can cut wasted runs.
routines.content:
Weekly routine cost check across the owner's whole Grok Bot fleet. Read-only: change nothing, edit no routine, and wake no other bot.

List every bot's live routines (enabled, with a schedule or trigger) from the routine definitions and recent run outcomes you can read. For each, record the owning bot, name, schedule or trigger, runs per week, and the share of last week's runs that were quiet (found nothing) or failed. Flag any routine over 100 runs a week, or over 80% quiet or failed, and propose one fix: an event trigger where a real one exists, a cheap change check before the full run, or a lower frequency. Also note any cron that sets both day-of-month and day-of-week (cron fires when either matches), and any plain-text secret in a routine prompt. Use runs and percentages only; never invent token or dollar figures, and label estimates.

Send the result to the owner in this chat. Lead with total fleet runs per week, compared with last week if known, then list only flagged routines with their fix. If nothing is flagged, send one line with the total and say nothing is flagged.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 7 9 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Weekly hours-saved report
routines.description: Fires Sunday evening to estimate the hours each bot saved that week and flag busy bots that save little as spend-cut candidates.
routines.content:
Weekly hours-saved report for the owner. Hand the work to one background worker to keep usage low: no browser and no cloud agents. For each bot active in the last 7 days, read only that week's transcript tail and stop paging at the week boundary. Count finished deliverables only (a result, file, draft, booking, or fix the owner received); skip acks, FYIs, bot-to-bot relays, and failed or abandoned work. Estimate manual time per deliverable: quick lookup 5 min; research summary 30 min; draft message or doc 20 min; form or web task 15 min; code or app build 2 h; image job 45 min; a routine run that surfaced something useful 5 min (quiet runs 0). Cap each at 3 h. Subtract about 2 min of the owner's time per message, review, or approval. Round net hours to 0.5 and label them estimates. Show an activity count per bot (turns plus helper, browser, and cloud-agent runs), labeled activity, not dollars; add an account-wide dollar line only if the owner gave a usage figure that week. Output one table (bot, deliverables, estimated hours saved, activity, note) plus the top 3 and bottom 3, and flag any bot with high activity and about 0 hours as a spend-cut candidate. Leave out inactive bots. Send the result to the owner in this chat. If the whole week had no activity, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 37 19 * * 0`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
